key_insight: Raising argon flow from 1600 to 1800 L/h during air plasma spraying produced thicker, denser NiCrFeBSiC coatings with better tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing plasma-spray gas flow can improve coating quality and wear resistance without changing the coating chemistry, which is useful for surface protection applications.
method: Air plasma sprayed self-fluxing NiCrFeBSiC coatings at two argon flow rates: 1600 and 1800 L/h.
Characterized microstructure, thickness, porosity, microhardness, elastic modulus, adhesion, and wear behavior.
Used ball-on-disk tribology and scratch testing to compare performance.
evidence_signal: At 1800 L/h, coating thickness roughly doubled, porosity roughly halved, and the friction coefficient dropped to about 0.107, while critical load remained similar but failure was more gradual.
watch_item: The improvement is shown only for two argon-flow settings, so broader process windows and long-term durability still need validation.
paper_title: EFFECT OF ARGON FLOW RATE DURING AIR PLASMA SPRAYING ON THE STRUCTURE AND PROPERTIES OF NICRFEBSIC COATINGS
